results.quote: Across three multi-hop QA workloads with _K_ from 10 to 1600, ConStore reduces end-to-end retrieval latency over the best per-document-read baseline by up to 48% on DiskANN and 25% on SPANN.

results.problem: Disk-based ANNS end-to-end retrieval latency (large-scale SIFT)
results.bound: 42\%\text{ on SIFT100M and }40\%\text{ on SIFT1B for DiskANN; }30\text{--}43\%\text{ for SPANN at }K=1600
results.quote: At recall targets 0.90/0.95, DiskANN’s latency reductions reach 42% on SIFT100M and 40% on SIFT1B; SPANN saves 30-43% at _K_=1600 across the two scales.
With both optimizations, RPAG lowers fetch latency by 45-47% over Random and 19-22% over K-Means using the same optimized fetch path.
The runtime representation is a packed pair of 32-bit integers, so the map costs 8 B per document, roughly one percent of the embedding-side ANN index memory in our workloads.
At those same operating points, ConStore lowers device read bandwidth by 23.4% on DiskANN and 19.7% on SPANN.
ConStore increases sustainable offered QPS by 20% on DiskANN and 12.5% on SPANN.
At the baselines’ highest sustainable rates , P99 latency is lower by factors of 1.46\(\times\) and 2.90\(\times\).

results.bound: 2.5\text{--}12\%\text{ of the corpus vs. }15\text{--}26\%\text{ for periodic full rebuilds}
results.quote: Across the seven scenarios in Figure 16(b), WASR rewrites 2.5-12% of the corpus, compared with 15-26% for periodic full rebuilds.
